3 CONT FIFTH CIRCUIT COURT
3 CONT (#1-206, 1852-1899)
3 CONT DIVORCE: FIFTH CIRCUIT COURT
3 CONT This is a personal name index to the Divorce Case Files of the Fifth Circuit Court dated 1852-1899.
3 CONT This index is arranged alphabetically by the married couple's last names. Both the husband's and wife's names are indexed. The Fifth Circuit Court Divorce case file number precedes the names of the parties. The following is a sample index entry.
3 CONT CASE NUMBER       NAMES OF PLAINTIFF &amp; DEFENDANT
3 CONT          119                    Namore, Pedro vs. Namore, Marie Carolina
3 CONT In many of the index entries a (k) or (w) follows one of the names.
3 CONT                  (k) stands for kane, or male
3 CONT                  (w) stands for wahine, or female
3 CONT The Hawaii State Archives holdings for Divorce case files begin with case 1 and end with 206. Divorce case files have been microfilmed and cataloged as MFL 60, available in Hawaii State Archives Microform Research Room.
3 CONT To look at a divorce, please note MFL 60 and the divorce number preceding the name of the individual you are researching.
3 CONT For more information about Divorce Case Files of the Fifth Circuit Court, please refer to the Inventory of Records of the Judiciary located in the Hawaii State Archives Research Room.

2 PAGE Family History Library; Book 929.273, T839g
2 DATA
3 TEXT Thomas Tupper, son of Henry Tupper, was born 1570, died 28 Mar 1676, married first 24 Apr 1622, Katherine Gator. Issue:
4 CONT        Katherine Tupper, born 31 Jan 1623, died 4 June 1676
4 CONT        Robert Tupper, died 1630. 
4 CONT Thomas married second, 25 Jan 1628, Susan Turner. Issue:
4 CONT       Thomas Tupper, died in infancy.
4 CONT       Robert Tupper, baptized 3 Nov 1633.
4 CONT Thomas married third, 21 Dec 1634, Mrs Anne Hodgson. Issue:
4 CONT       Thomas Tupper, born 16 Jan 1638, died 26 Apr 1706.
4 CONT Thomas Tupper was born in Sussex county, England. As a young man he was a leather worker, but by 1621, had become a sailor. We know of three sea voyages he made, one of which was to Plymouth Colony in 1624, when he stayed over a year and returned t
4 CONC o England with a cargo of furs and rare woods.
4 CONT We do not know exactly when he finally settled in New England, but it may have been before 1628, as in that year there is a cloudy account of the marriage of Thomas Tupper to Susan Turner at Topsfield, Mass. The first undisputable reference to hi
4 CONC m in New England is the account of his marriage to Anne Hodgson at Ipswich, Mass., in 1634. We next find him in Sandwich, Mass., in 1637, with the two surviving children from his first two marriages, and his third wife, Anne, who became the mothe
4 CONC r of Thomas Tupper.
4 CONT (His daughter) Katherine Tupper married in Sandwich, Mass., and had issue, but they did not bear the Tupper name. Robert Tupper married but returned to England, so the children of Thomas are the only ones to carry on the family name in this country
4 CONC .
4 CONT Sandwich, Mass., (on Cape Cod) became the Tupper residence for many years. Here, in 1637, Thomas built a house and it was so well built that it served for 267 years, finally being destroyed by fire. Thomas was very religious and labored diligentl
4 CONC y at being a missionary to the Indians. After his death, his son, Thomas, carried on this work. Thomas was sometimes called "Captain", but this was only a courtesy as he was never was a captain. His son, Thomas, was also called "Captain", and right
4 CONC ly so as he was a captain in the local militia.
4 CONT Anne Hodgson was born about 1588 and died 4 June 1676. Both she and Thomas died in Sandwich and are buried there on the Tupper homestead at Sandwich.

1 _META <metadataxml><content><line>&lt;p&gt;Alexander P. Hussey,carpenter and cabinet maker, son of Joseph Starbuck Hussey and Lydia E. Pollard Hussey, was born April 14, 1825 on Nantucket Island, and traveled to Hawaii where he fathered two well-known fa
2 CONC milies on the Big Island (Hawaii Island) and is remembered by many descendants. It is erroneously reported in Nantucket records that Alexander P. Hussey "died single."&lt;br&gt;&lt;br&gt;He left New England on th ship 'Columbus' of Fairhaven, Massa
2 CONC chusetts, which is across the harbor from New Bedford, Massachusetts. This ship was under the command of Capt. Fish (no first name given) and sailed from the above port November 13, 1843 for the Northwest Pacific ocean for whaling. The agents of th
2 CONC e ship were Gibbs and Jenney of New Bedford, Massachusetts. After a very successful voyage of 23 months the 'Columbus' arrived in Hawaii October 12, 1845 with 800 barrels of sperm oil, 2,400 barrels of whale oil and 14,000 pounds of whale bone. I
2 CONC t remained there until November 24, 1845 when it sailed for home, arriving in Fairhaven April 13, 1846. The records show only this one trip from Fairhaven to Hawaii for Alexander Hussey.&lt;br&gt;&lt;br&gt;Alexander eventually settled in Waipio Val
2 CONC ley on the Hamakua coast of Hawaii Island. This valley was once the royal center for many of Hawaii's early kings. There he married Manaiakalani ("Manaia"), daughter of the ali'i (chief) Opunui, who had served as a warrior and ambassador for firs
2 CONC t monarch of a united Hawaii, Kamehameha the Great during his conquest of the islands. In 1862, Alexander Hussey and Manaia had one child: a boy named George Alika Hussey. "Alika" is the Hawaiian for "Alexander". A historical study of Waipio Valle
2 CONC y by the Bishop Museum refers to George Alika Hussey as "Alika Hussey". He became a respected taro grower in the Valley. His granddaughter, Emily Kaelehiwa Hussey married Nawai Kekoolani. George Alika Hussey and his son, George Alika Hussey, Jr. ar
2 CONC e buried in Waipio Valley at the family cemetery located on the land he recieved from his grandfather, the chief Opunui, now held by the Kekoolani Family Trust. A book entitled "The Husseys of Waipio Valley" by Amy Kekoolani Akao, George's great gr
2 CONC anddaughter, documents the expansion of the Hussey family of Waipio Valley.&lt;br&gt;&lt;br&gt;Alexander Hussey recieved a commission to build a church in Kohala, on the other side of the island. He left Waipio Valley and relocated to Kohala tempor
2 CONC arily, leaving Manaia and her son George Alika Hussey at Waipio Valley with the Opunui family. In Kohala, he met and married another Hawaiian woman Kaai-Kaula-Kalei-Kau-Welaha-Makanoe Naweluokekikipaaa (or Makanoe Ka'aikaula). Fourteen children wer
2 CONC e born to them, and in 1979 over 400 descendants had been recorded from this Kohala branch of the Hussey family alone.&lt;br&gt;&lt;br&gt;Alexander Pollard Hussey died in Kohala on May 10, 1896 at 77 years of age, the patriarch of a large and wel
2 CONC l respected Hawaiian family. He was buried at Niulii, Kohala, Hawaii.&lt;/p&gt;</line></content></metadataxml>

2 TITL Arrival of Hussey Family into Hawaii
1 RIN 92c300a1-563f-4a00-91ef-3545fae7ca30
1 _META <metadataxml><content><line>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 12px; font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;"&gt;(NOTE: Some facts below contradict what is included in other "stories" on Ancestry -- I am just sharing word-for-word as found.)&lt
2 CONC ;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</line><line>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 12px;"&gt;Alexander P. Hussey, carpenter and cabinet maker, son of Joseph Starbuck Hussey and Lydia E. Pollard Husse
2 CONC y, was born April 14, 1825 on Nantucket Island, and traveled to Hawaii where he fathered two well-known families on the Big Island (Hawaii Island) and is remembered by many descendants. It is erroneously reported in Nantucket records that Alexande
2 CONC r P. Hussey "died single."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</line><line>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 12px;"&gt;He left New England on th ship 'Columbus' of Fairhaven, Massachu
2 CONC setts, which is across the harbor from New Bedford, Massachusetts. This ship was under the command of Capt. Fish (no first name given) and sailed from the above port November 13, 1843 for the Northwest Pacific ocean for whaling. The agents of the s
2 CONC hip were Gibbs and Jenney of New Bedford, Massachusetts. After a very successful voyage of 23 months the 'Columbus' arrived in Hawaii October 12, 1845 with 800 barrels of sperm oil, 2,400 barrels of whale oil and 14,000 pounds of whale bone. It rem
2 CONC ained there until November 24, 1845 when it sailed for home, arriving in Fairhaven April 13, 1846. The records show only this one trip from Fairhaven to Hawaii for Alexander Hussey.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</line><line>&lt;p&gt;&lt;spa
2 CONC n style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 12px;"&gt;Alexander eventually settled in Waipio Valley on the Hamakua coast of Hawaii Island. This valley was once the royal center for many of Hawaii's early kings
2 CONC . There he married Manaiakalani ("Manaia"), daughter of the ali'i (chief) Opunui, who had served as a warrior and ambassador for first monarch of a united Hawaii, Kamehameha the Great during his conquest of the islands. In 1862, Alexander Hussey an
2 CONC d Manaia had one child: a boy named George Alika Hussey. "Alika" is the Hawaiian for "Alexander". A historical study of Waipio Valley by the Bishop Museum refers to George Alika Hussey as "Alika Hussey". He became a respected taro grower in the Val
2 CONC ley. His granddaughter, Emily Kaelehiwa Hussey married Nawai Kekoolani. George Alika Hussey and his son, George Alika Hussey, Jr. are buried in Waipio Valley at the family cemetery located on the land he recieved from his grandfather, the chief Opu
2 CONC nui, now held by the Kekoolani Family Trust. A book entitled "The Husseys of Waipio Valley" by Amy Kekoolani Akao, George's great granddaughter, documents the expansion of the Hussey family of Waipio Valley.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</lin
2 CONC e><line>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 12px;"&gt;Alexander Hussey recieved a commission to build a church in Kohala, on the other side of the island. He left Waipio Valley and relo
2 CONC cated to Kohala temporarily, leaving Manaia and her son George Alika Hussey at Waipio Valley with the Opunui family. In Kohala, he met and married another Hawaiian woman Kaai-Kaula-Kalei-Kau-Welaha-Makanoe Naweluokekikipaaa (or Makanoe Ka'aikaula)
2 CONC . Fourteen children were born to them, and in 1979 over 400 descendants had been recorded from this Kohala branch of the Hussey family alone.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</line><line>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;</line><line>&lt;p&gt;&lt;spa
2 CONC n style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 12px;"&gt;Alexander Pollard Hussey died in Kohala on May 10, 1896 at 77 years of age, the patriarch of a large and well respected Hawaiian family. He was buried at N
2 CONC iulii, Kohala, Hawaii.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</line><line>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 12px;"&gt;Source:&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-fami

2 TITL Henry Hartwell K. Blake (1874 - 1948) - Find A Grave Memorial
1 RIN ab2248e9-8138-4a59-b2d2-3a951772cacd
1 DATE 05 Feb 2014 
1 PLAC Koloa, Kauai
1 _DSCR "BLAKE, HENRY, lawyer, Koloa, Kauai; born in Koloa, July 31, 1874; son of Alva and Kaonohi (Kuaalu) Blake; married Margarette Miller at Koloa, Nov. 20, 1902; six children: Eleanor, Emma, Juliette, Bernard, Hartwell, and Charles. Educated Hilo Board
2 CONC ing School, 1884-91; Kamehameha School, Honolulu, 1891-93. Was teacher at reformatory school, Honolulu, 1893-94; deputy tax assessor and collector, Koloa, 1894-1904; superintendent Koloa water works; deputy sheriff, Koloa, 1906-16; elected auditor
2 CONC , County of Kauai, 1919, which position he still holds. Member Kaumualii Chapter, Order of Kamehameha; Court Waialeale No. 9251, A. O. F. ; Kauai Chamber of Commerce." --[From MEN OF HAWAII A BIOGRAPHICAL REFERENCE LIBRARY. COMPLETE AND AUTHENTIC
2 CONC , OF THE MEN OF NOTE AND SUBSTANTIAL ACHIEVEMENT IN THE HAWAIIAN ISLANDS]
2 CONT 
2 CONT Second article on Henry Blake...
2 CONT 
2 CONT "A member of one of Kaua‘i's oldest kama‘aina families, Henry K. Blake was born in Wailana, Koloa on July 31, 1874 — the 18th day of the Hawaiian lunar month — one of four children of Alva and Kaonohiulaokala Kuaalu Blake. Blake was educated at Kol
2 CONC oa School, Hilo Boarding School and Malumalu School, Kaua‘i, which was founded by Dr. Jared Smith and his sister, Juliette Smith, in 1890. Until it was razed in 1920, Malumalu School stood on the south side of Hulemalu Road, about a quarter-mile ea
2 CONC st of the intersection of Puhi and Hulemalu roads. Blake also attended Kamehameha Schools and graduated with its second graduating class in 1893. Since that time, four successive generations of his descendants have attended Kamehameha Schools. Foll
2 CONC owing his graduation, Blake taught school at Keone‘ula Correctional School in Kapalama, O‘ahu for one year before returning to Kaua‘i, where he was appointed Deputy Tax Assessor and Collector in Koloa (1894-1904) and Superintendent of Koloa Water W
2 CONC orks (1900-1912). From 1906 to 1916, he was elected to successive terms as Deputy Sheriff of Koloa District. In 1919 he was elected as auditor of the County of Kaua‘i. Thereafter, he successfully petitioned the courts to grant him an attorney's lic
2 CONC ense and subsequently became a longtime judge for the Koloa District. Throughout his life, Blake was a member of the old Koloa Hawaiian Church. His father was one of the carpenters who built the original church in 1859. Henry K. Blake was also a li
2 CONC felong friend and confidant of Prince Jonah Kuhio Kalanianaole Piikoi. He and Prince Kuhio would spend many an afternoon on the spacious lanai of Blake's Koloa home, talking, smoking cigars, and drinking ale. He and his first wife, Eunice Kameeuala
2 CONC ni Manoi, had one daughter, Kealoha Blake. His second marriage was to Margaret Kahaipiilani Miller of Koloa in 1902. They had six children: Eleanor Kaaikauilani, Emma Kaleimakalii, Juliette Kaonohiulauokala, Bernard Kahikonamoku, Hartwell Kawahineh
2 CONC elelani and Charles Kaumualii. Judge Henry K. Blake died in September of 1948."

2 CONC milies on the Big Island (Hawaii Island) and is remembered by many descendants. It is erroneously reported in Nantucket records that Alexander P. Hussey "died single."&lt;br&gt;&lt;br&gt;He left New England on th ship 'Columbus' of Fairhaven, Massa
2 CONC chusetts, which is across the harbor from New Bedford, Massachusetts. This ship was under the command of Capt. Fish (no first name given) and sailed from the above port November 13, 1843 for the Northwest Pacific ocean for whaling. The agents of th
2 CONC e ship were Gibbs and Jenney of New Bedford, Massachusetts. After a very successful voyage of 23 months the 'Columbus' arrived in Hawaii October 12, 1845 with 800 barrels of sperm oil, 2,400 barrels of whale oil and 14,000 pounds of whale bone. I
2 CONC t remained there until November 24, 1845 when it sailed for home, arriving in Fairhaven April 13, 1846. The records show only this one trip from Fairhaven to Hawaii for Alexander Hussey.&lt;br&gt;&lt;br&gt;Alexander eventually settled in Waipio Val
2 CONC ley on the Hamakua coast of Hawaii Island. This valley was once the royal center for many of Hawaii's early kings. There he married Manaiakalani ("Manaia"), daughter of the ali'i (chief) Opunui, who had served as a warrior and ambassador for firs
2 CONC t monarch of a united Hawaii, Kamehameha the Great during his conquest of the islands. In 1862, Alexander Hussey and Manaia had one child: a boy named George Alika Hussey. "Alika" is the Hawaiian for "Alexander". A historical study of Waipio Valle
2 CONC y by the Bishop Museum refers to George Alika Hussey as "Alika Hussey". He became a respected taro grower in the Valley. His granddaughter, Emily Kaelehiwa Hussey married Nawai Kekoolani. George Alika Hussey and his son, George Alika Hussey, Jr. ar
2 CONC e buried in Waipio Valley at the family cemetery located on the land he recieved from his grandfather, the chief Opunui, now held by the Kekoolani Family Trust. A book entitled "The Husseys of Waipio Valley" by Amy Kekoolani Akao, George's great gr
2 CONC anddaughter, documents the expansion of the Hussey family of Waipio Valley.&lt;br&gt;&lt;br&gt;Alexander Hussey recieved a commission to build a church in Kohala, on the other side of the island. He left Waipio Valley and relocated to Kohala tempor
2 CONC arily, leaving Manaia and her son George Alika Hussey at Waipio Valley with the Opunui family. In Kohala, he met and married another Hawaiian woman Kaai-Kaula-Kalei-Kau-Welaha-Makanoe Naweluokekikipaaa (or Makanoe Ka'aikaula). Fourteen children wer
2 CONC e born to them, and in 1979 over 400 descendants had been recorded from this Kohala branch of the Hussey family alone.&lt;br&gt;&lt;br&gt;Alexander Pollard Hussey died in Kohala on May 10, 1896 at 77 years of age, the patriarch of a large and wel
